summary: Describes the computer graphics setup in the UCLA computer science department in 1971. The hardware includes two Imlac PDS-1 consoles, each with 8K 16-bit words of memory, and a DEC 340 display with a light pen, a Rand Tablet and a Lincoln Wand. It was written for the network graphics meeting in RFC 134.

plainLanguage.summary: UCLA describes the graphics machines and programs available in its computer science department. The report also lists planned changes to its equipment and software.

subtitle: A snapshot of graphics equipment and software at UCLA in 1971.

tldr.problem: The network graphics community needed information about the equipment and software available at different sites.
tldr.mechanism: UCLA describes its Imlac PDS-1 consoles, DEC 340 display station, associated input devices and graphics programs.
tldr.outcome: The report shares UCLA's then-current capabilities and plans for expanding them.

sections.title: Graphics Equipment
sections.content:
UCLA had two Imlac PDS-1 graphics consoles, each with 8K 16-bit words of memory and a vertically mounted display. It also had a DEC 340 Display Station with a light pen, Rand Tablet and Lincoln Wand.

A display processor drove the DEC 340 and read its instructions from XDS Sigma 7 memory through a dedicated port.
sections.plainLanguage: UCLA had two Imlac graphics consoles and a DEC 340 display station. The DEC 340 worked with a light pen, tablet and wand.

sections.title: Software and Graphics Programs
sections.content:
The Imlac consoles used supplied text and graphics support software as alphanumeric and limited graphics terminals at 1200 baud. UCLA had not yet developed its own PDS-1 software.

For the DEC 340, UCLA had library routines that worked with FORTRAN. Programs included MOSAIC for exploring images from polar-coordinate equations, FISHEYE for viewing large images on a small screen, and MOVIE for describing animated sequences.
sections.plainLanguage: The Imlac consoles could show text and limited graphics. UCLA's DEC 340 programs could create images, display large pictures in a compressed view and make animated sequences.

sections.title: Planned Development
sections.content:
UCLA planned to add a mouse and keyset to the PDS-1 systems and try programs developed at other sites. It also planned an assembler and considered a graphics library for FORTRAN or other high-level languages.

The group intended eventually to make the DEC 340 hardware and software available through its SEX timesharing system.
sections.plainLanguage: UCLA planned to add input devices and software to the Imlac consoles. It also hoped to connect the DEC 340 facilities to its timesharing system.
